entries.name: audit-backlog-ado
entries.description: Audits the Azure DevOps product backlog for hygiene, story quality, and refinement readiness — identifying items that are too large, missing acceptance criteria, stale, unestimated, or out of priority order. entries.name: audit-sprint-ado
entries.description: Audits a completed or in-progress Azure DevOps sprint against Scrum and ADO best practices — checks Sprint Goal presence, work item hygiene, state transitions, field completeness, capacity tracking, and Definition of Done compliance. Surfaces findings with severity levels and offers to post a summary to the ADO wiki or add comments to specific work items. Use when anyone says things like "audit our sprint in ADO", "review the sprint in Azure DevOps", "check our ADO sprint health", "are our work items following best practices", or "sprint health check". Don't use for Jira, Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, or Retrospective. Requires an Azure DevOps MCP connection.

entries.name: audit-sprint-jira
entries.description: Audits a completed or in-progress Jira sprint against Scrum and Jira best practices — checks Sprint Goal presence, issue hygiene, workflow transitions, field completeness, story point coverage, and sub-task consistency. Surfaces findings with severity levels and offers to add comments to specific issues or export a summary report. Use when anyone says things like "audit our sprint in Jira", "review the Jira sprint", "check our Jira sprint health", "are our issues following best practices", or "sprint health check in Jira". Don't use for Azure DevOps — use audit-sprint-ado instead. Don't use for Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, or Retrospective. Requires a Jira MCP connection.

entries.name: audit-sprint-retrospective-ado
entries.description: Reads an Azure DevOps retrospective — from the ADO Retrospectives extension board, a wiki page, or retro-tagged work items — and produces a structured summary of what the team said, identifies patterns and recurring themes, audits whether action items are properly tracked as work items with owners, and generates concrete suggestions. Use when anyone says things like "summarize our retro", "audit the retrospective in ADO", "what were the action items from the retro", "review the team's retrospective board", "check our retro follow-up", or "did we capture everything from the retro". Don't use for facilitating a retrospective in real time, Jira projects, or general Scrum questions.

entries.name: audit-user-story
entries.description: Audits an existing user story against Scrum best practices — checks INVEST criteria, story format, acceptance criteria quality, and Definition of Ready compliance. Raises findings with clear severity levels and offers to post the audit as a comment on the work item for the Product Owner or PM to act on. Use when anyone says things like "audit this story", "review this user story", "is this story ready", "check this PBI", "does this story meet best practices", or pastes a story and asks for feedback. Don't use for creating new stories, sprint planning, or general Scrum questions. Works with ADO, Jira, or a pasted story.

Every state change lands in the actions journal with an actor and review state; agents act provisionally and the editor reviews a ranked queue afterward (acknowledge or overturn, signed). On invocation reads full posture (screens with yield, leads, dispositions, unreviewed actions). Hands off to track-investigation on promotion, and to sweep-for-screens when the live slate is exhausted. Use when running the newsroom, going fishing, surfacing or triaging leads, reviewing autonomous actions, promoting a lead, or building a derived table. Trigger phrases: run the newsroom, newsroom status, go fish, surface leads, triage leads, review actions, promote a lead, check posture.

entries.name: ingest-to-sqlite

Encodes a verifiable-ingestion methodology — preserve the source's own IDs as keys, store money and numbers both raw and parsed, fold controlled vocabularies into reference tables, add FTS5 for free text, stamp every fact row with a source key or URL, make rebuilds source-scoped and idempotent, and validate by reconciling row counts and foreign keys against the raw source. Use when building a database or ETL pipeline from raw data files, designing a SQLite schema, normalizing nested data, or making query results traceable for journalism, research, or analytics. Includes a generic database verifier.

entries.name: sweep-for-screens

Encodes the contrast taxonomy (six ways a lead can deviate from a baseline, crossed with the corpus's grains) that partitions idea space across a scout fleet, fleet run-economics (pilot-first, probe budgets, tier models by fleet size, hard token ceilings), and the beat-nomination discipline for using outside reporting to aim the corpus without letting it into evidence. Use when sweeping for new screen ideas, designing a screen, expanding fishing capability, proposing a derived table, or running a fleet sweep. Trigger phrases: sweep for leads, design new screens, expand the newsroom, run a sweep, propose a derived table.

entries.name: track-investigation

Defines durable on-disk case files (hypothesis, sourced evidence, running log), a layered data architecture that keeps the immutable source database, shared rebuildable derived tables, and case-local artifacts separate and reproducible. entries.name: lw-case-studies
entries.description: The case layer - how to take a finished lyric apart and what three working lyricists say about their own habits (案例与拆解). A fixed twelve-row worksheet for dissecting any song, keyed to the library's own fields so every finding lands in a skill instead of staying an impression; the rule that a real lyric is read from the middle outward, not from the theme down; what Yao Qian, Zhang Li and Hong Yuan each say about opening lines, restraint, revision, rhyme width, colloquial versus literary diction and how much to leave the composer, plus the four places they openly disagree and how to pick a side; worked dissections of songs the sources analyse in full, including one song two of them discuss independently; and the failure patterns they name - flat, scattered, overlong, bland, blunt, bare, stuffed. Use when studying a lyric you admire, when you need a real example of a technique, when a draft feels wrong and you want a model to compare against, or when asked to critique a song. 案例、拆解、词评、作品分析、词人自述、改稿对照。

entries.name: lw-chinese-style
entries.description: The Chinese-style layer for lyric writing (中国风歌词). What makes a lyric read as 中国风 rather than merely decorated - the vocabulary families it draws on (place, dynasty, object, craft, plant), the sixteen rhetorical devices Fang Wen-shan catalogues inside his own lyrics, each with a book example and a failure condition, why every image must belong to one material world and how one out-of-period object breaks it, the four grades of borrowing from classical verse and where borrowing becomes copying, what to do when the listener will not catch the allusion, what the words promise the arrangement when they name an instrument, and the three ways this style usually dies - ornament with no event, images unrelated to what the song says, and archaism for its own sake. Use when writing or auditing a 中国风 or 古风 lyric, when a draft is full of beautiful old words but says nothing, when checking an allusion, when images from different eras collide, or when the words name an instrument. 中国风、古风、典故、化用、文字游戏、修辞、意象成套、方文山、穿帮。

entries.name: lw-english
entries.description: The English language layer for lyric writing (英文词的重音与节拍对齐). Word stress is fixed inside a polysyllabic word, so the melody bends to the word and never the reverse; stressed syllables belong on stressed notes, which keeps the natural shape of the language; line length is counted in stressed syllables, not total syllables; common meter and its 4-3 stress lines; long syllables want long notes and the contour should track the sentence's intonation; where the breath falls, how phrase length accelerates a section, what enjambment costs; what gonna, wanna and 'em do to the count; why the, of and and must not land on a downbeat; and the mistakes a Chinese-speaking writer makes in English. Use when writing or checking English lyrics, fitting English words to a melody, when a sung line sounds mispronounced, when counting syllables, or when a line will not fit the bar. 英文作词、英文歌词、重音、节拍对齐、音节数、prosody、phrasing、气口、重音落错、唱不进小节。

entries.name: lw-imagery
entries.description: The imagery layer - how to find concrete nouns and make them a system (意象与具体名词). Object writing and the seven senses, the ten-minute timed practice, why abstract nouns are the most direct AI fingerprint and how to build the forbidden list, how to check that a lyric is not all sight, why a set of images must belong to one physical world instead of being piled up at random, simile versus metaphor and how to spot and replace a dead one, and how one object recurs with a shifting meaning. Use when a lyric feels vague or generic but the words look fine, when every noun in a draft is a concept, when you cannot find images, when images are pretty but unrelated, when a metaphor sounds borrowed, or when LYR-LINT check 2 fails. 意象、具体名词、抽象词、object writing、物体写作、五感、七感、比喻、明喻、暗喻、通感、陈词、死喻、词太泛、找不到意象。

entries.name: lw-japanese
entries.description: The Japanese language layer for lyric writing (日文词的モーラ与符割り). The counting unit is the mora, not the kana or the syllable - the small tsu, the moraic n and the long vowel each take a beat, a palatalized pair takes one; one kana per note is the default, and the same melody remaps itself when the words change; every word carries a pitch-accent contour, and a melody that fights it gets the line heard as a different sentence; fuwari, the mapping of kana to notes; bunsetsu segmentation and where a line may break; ji-amari and ji-tarazu as deliberate mismatch; the four ways to fix a melody when the counts do not fit; why Japanese rhyme is weak and how shichigo-cho slips in unnoticed; the lyrics-first and music-first routes; and the iron rule for English words inside a Japanese song. Use when writing or checking Japanese lyrics, fitting kana to an existing melody, counting morae, when a sung line is misheard as another word, or when the words will not sit on the notes. 日文作词、日语歌词、モーラ、拍数、符割り、字余り、字足らず、音高重音、七五調。

entries.name: lw-korean
entries.description: The Korean language layer for lyric writing (韩文词的音节与받침). One hangul block is one syllable is one note by default - unlike Japanese, a final consonant takes no beat of its own. The batchim (받침, syllable-final consonant) is the subject here; single and double batchim, the seven representative finals, and why a syllable closing on a stop is the wrong place for a long note, a phrase-end hold or a section peak. Liaison (연음) moves a batchim onto the next block, so the sung syllable boundary is not the written one, which moves every breath, caesura and rhyme landing. Plus the sound changes that rewrite a line between paper and voice (nasalization, tensification, aspiration, palatalization, elision, insertion, vowel harmony); why Korean has no tone and no word stress; how Korean rhyme differs from the Mandarin che. Use when writing or checking Korean lyrics, fitting hangul to a melody, counting syllables, or picking a word for a held note. 韩文作词、韩语歌词、받침、收音、连音、音变、音节数、K-pop 填词。

entries.name: lw-mandarin
entries.description: The Mandarin language layer for lyric writing (普通话作词的语言层). What Chinese as a language adds to the job; tone is phonemic, so the melody that enters a syllable can change which word is heard; one character is one syllable, so syllable count is character count; the thirteen rhyme families (十三辙) with their finals, example characters, wide-versus-narrow reach and loudness grades; how to pick a rhyme family, when to switch, and which families borrow from each other; level-and-oblique (平仄) and how much looser a lyric is than classical verse; the two- and three-character feet that make a Chinese line scan; and what makes a line easy or hard to sing. Use when writing or checking Mandarin lyrics, when choosing or changing a rhyme family, when a line is a tongue-twister or a high note lands on a closed vowel, when someone asks what 十三辙 is, or when LYR-LINT check 8 says the song sits on one or two wide families. 普通话、中文作词、十三辙、辙口、韵部、平仄、字调、易唱、绕口、开口音闭口音、什么是十三辙。

entries.name: lw-musical-theatre
entries.description: Theatre and musical-theatre lyric writing (剧场与音乐剧唱词). How a song becomes an action instead of a pause, how to make the words sound like the character rather than the lyricist, and what Sondheim's three principles - Content Dictates Form, Less Is More, God Is in the Details, all in the service of clarity - actually change in a draft. Covers character diction by vocabulary, syntax, schooling and period; first-person versus narrator; the price of repetition and the function of perfect rhyme on a stage; the seam between song and dialogue; Sondheim's catalogue of his own faults; and a transfer table for which rules a pop lyric should also obey. Use when writing a song for a character in a play or musical, when a song feels like a pause in the story, when two characters sound alike, when turning a scene into a song, or when deciding whether a theatre rule applies to a pop lyric. 音乐剧、剧场、角色唱词、戏剧、推进剧情、Sondheim、唱词与对白。

entries.name: lw-narrative
entries.description: Who is speaking, when they are speaking, and how much they are allowed to know (歌词的叙事层). The three narrative fields every lyric must fill - point of view, tense anchor, and the one thing deliberately left unsaid - with the cost of each person, the risk of mixing pronouns mid-song and the few shifts that actually work, how present/past/future change the listener's distance, why a fixed moment limits what the speaker can know (write the symptom, not the conclusion), why a completed emotional arc (hurt - peace - blessing) is a machine fingerprint, and how a story lyric advances through scene, turn and cost. Use when a draft has no speaker, when you cannot tell who is being addressed, when pronouns drift between sections, when the timeline is half memory and half now, when a lyric resolves everything and leaves nothing hanging, when writing a story song, or when LYR-LINT check 5 or 6 fails. 视角、人称、时间、时态、留白、不解决、叙事、故事型歌词、没有说话人、谁在说话、情绪走完整。

entries.name: lw-song-intent
entries.description: The gate you must pass before writing a single line (动笔前必填). Five questions that force an actual choice - which kind of song this is (attitudinal, situational, narrative, or expository, and why the default is not narrative), the one thing it says, who it is said to, at what moment, and the one photographable object that runs through it - with the failure mode each question catches, the downstream choices the song type fixes (person, voice, repetition budget), how to tell a real answer from a filled-in one, and why this gate exists at all (AI-written lyrics are not bad at words, they are written by nobody). Use when starting any lyric, when a draft feels generic but you cannot say why, when every song comes out as a story, when a song is trying to say two things, or when LYR-LINT check 1 fails. 立意、动笔前必填、歌的类型、态度型、情境型、叙事型、说理型、只说一件事、对谁说、锚定物件、重复预算、写不出来、太泛。

entries.name: lw-structure
entries.description: The structural layer of a lyric (词的结构层) - what each section is for and what it must not say, which song form to pick, where the title lands and how often it comes back, and how line counts, line lengths and rhyme placement make a section feel finished or still owing something. Covers verse / pre-chorus / chorus / bridge / refrain functions, central versus developmental sections, AABA and verse-chorus and verse-refrain forms, the five structural parameters (balance, pace, flow, closure, closure type), the five hook-placement strategies, and the deliberate asymmetry that keeps a lyric from sounding machine-made. entries.name: chekhov-dramaturgy
entries.description: Writing plays and screenplays in the Chekhovian mode (契诃夫戏剧法) — distilled from the complete plays (没有父亲的人/普拉东诺夫, 伊凡诺夫, 林妖→万尼亚舅舅, 海鸥, 三姊妹, 樱桃园, nine one-acts) plus Chekhov's own letters, Stanislavsky's and Nemirovich-Danchenko's rehearsal notes and 焦菊隐/童道明 criticism. Covers the four-act mood-based structure without central climax, off-stage events, "correct answer stated in Act 1 and refused", the announced event that never happens, three-layer endings (hope monologue + nihilist line + household action), no-villain conflict with environment, every character's object and catchphrase, one-way love chains, half-step-off dialogue, philosophy cut by thirst, the shortest words for the deepest pain, stage-direction and sound discipline, and how Chekhov revised The Wood Demon into Uncle Vanya. Use when the user wants an ensemble drama, a "nothing happens" play, subtext-heavy dialogue, a family estate / provincial story, an anti-climactic structure, or asks how to "Chekhov-ize" a script.

Covers the "family member leaves" master plot, off-screen events / on-screen reactions, lie-driven plots, minimal-syllable confessions, go-between characters, faceless suitors, pillow-shot scene breaks, echoing objects, mirror characters, children's subplots as metaphor, displaced quarrels, the single-monologue rule, diminishing endings, Ozu's script format and stage-direction vocabulary. Use when the user wants to write a quiet family drama, a 小津风 / 侘寂 / 日常系 script, a story about marrying off a daughter, aging parents, or wants dialogue that says less and means more.

entries.name: supabase-postgres-best-practices

Load this skill BEFORE writing or changing anything that lives in a Postgres database: creating or altering tables and columns (including choosing column types), schema design, migrations and declarative schema files, RLS policies and the tests that verify them, indexes, triggers, database functions, queues and scheduled jobs (pg_cron, pgmq), vector/semantic search (pgvector), and restoring dumps (pg_restore) or importing data. Also load it when diagnosing slow queries, high CPU, timeouts, EXPLAIN plans, connection exhaustion, locking, bloat, or rows visible to the wrong user or tenant.
